html:
The Ticuna, who call themselves Magüta, are an Indigenous people of the upper Amazon, where Brazil, Colombia and Peru meet. They are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of the Amazon.

Their language is usually treated as an isolate, unrelated to its neighbours. They live in villages along the Solimões (the upper Amazon) and its side streams, fishing, farming manioc and making bark cloth and masks. Their best known ceremony is the coming of age festival for girls, which lasts several days.

When the Omagua (Kambeba) of the main river collapsed after contact, the Ticuna moved down from the side streams to the Amazon itself. The rubber boom brought forced labour. In 1988 loggers killed fourteen Ticuna at Capacete in Brazil. Their neighbours include the Yagua.
sum: The Ticuna, who call themselves Magüta, are an Indigenous people of the upper Amazon, where Brazil, Colombia and Peru meet. They are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of the Amazon.
